method: Each page was fetched on the check date and the statements the article relies on were located in the page text. Findings are paraphrased here; the pages themselves are the source. Nothing in the article is a quotation from these pages. The rule in the article's code block is our own.

definition_sources.name: LuxAlgo library: Inversion FVG
what_it_says: A fair value gap that failed and flipped roles; a bullish gap that price closes below becomes resistance, a bearish gap that price closes above becomes support.
A candle body closing through the far side is the common standard; a wick alone is usually read as a probe.
Conventions differ: some require the whole gap closed through, others a close beyond its midpoint.
The first return to the inverted zone is watched for rejection; the stop goes just beyond the far side; a reclaim invalidates the idea.
Describes an inversion as a hypothesis, not a guarantee, and notes that many inverted gaps are reclaimed on the first retest.
Gives no statistics and names no originator.

definition_sources.name: TradingView: Inversion Fair Value Gaps (IFVG) [LuxAlgo], open-source script
what_it_says: Says it is based on the inversion FVG concept by ICT.
Mitigation (what turns a gap into an inversion) is a close above or below the gap area against its bias.
Signals appear when price returns to an inversion zone and rejects; a 'Signal Preference' setting chooses wick or close for the signal.
An ATR multiplier setting filters gaps by width.
States that backtesting its historical signals is incorrect because it does not take the mitigation of inversion zones into account.
definition_sources.not_read: The Pine Script source was not read; only the description on the page.

definition_sources.name: Quantum Algo glossary: inversion fair value gap
what_it_says: A fair value gap that price has closed through; a failed bullish gap becomes resistance and a failed bearish gap support.
Requires a candle body to close completely beyond the far side; a close inside the gap is a partial fill and a wick through with a close back inside is a sweep.
Entry on the first retest, stop beyond the gap's far edge; advises caution on a second retest.
Says inversion gaps are central to the entry logic of an ICT model, without crediting anyone with inventing the concept.

naming.finding: 'Inversion fair value gap' (LuxAlgo library, LuxAlgo script, Quantum Algo) and 'inverse fair value gap' (for example the title of an FXOpen idea listed on TradingView's IFVG tag pages in a web search on the check date) are used for the same idea. We found no source that distinguishes them.
naming.caveat: The FXOpen page itself returned HTTP 404 at the address we tried, so nothing in the article is attributed to it.

origin.conclusion: No dated, written primary source for the term was found. The LuxAlgo script attributes the concept to ICT in one phrase; none of the three pages cites a lecture or a date. The article attributes the term to nobody in particular and no wording to Michael J. Huddleston.
